title: Driving Licence 2026: Apply Online, LL to Permanent DL
meta_description: Driving license 2026 - apply online via Parivahan portal, Learner's License, permanent DL, renewal, documents, driving test, RTO slot booking.

hero.one_liner: Get driving license online through Parivahan portal - Learner's License first, then permanent DL after practice and driving test at RTO

sections.heading: Driving Licence: LL First, Then Permanent DL
content: Getting a driving licence in India is a two-step process. You first get a Learner's Licence to practice, then a permanent Driving Licence after a road test.
The Learner's Licence, or LL, is valid for 6 months and needs you to pass a simple online test on traffic rules. You must drive with an L sign and a licensed driver beside you.
The permanent DL needs a practical driving test at the RTO. You can apply for it only after holding the LL for at least 30 days, and within 180 days.
Around 30 crore Indians hold a driving licence, yet many more drive without one, which is both illegal and risky.
Doing it properly is cheaper and faster than people expect, and the licence is your legal proof to drive anywhere in India.

sections.heading: Driving Licence: Key Numbers

sections.title: Apply on the Parivahan Sarathi Portal
sections.content:
All driving licence services run through the central Parivahan portal, with applications on sarathi.parivahan.gov.in. Every state uses the same system.

You apply online, upload documents, pay the fee, and book an RTO slot. After issue, your DL lives in the mParivahan app and DigiLocker as a legally valid copy.

sections.heading: Step 1: Get Your Learner's Licence

steps.title: Open Sarathi
steps.desc: Go to sarathi.parivahan.gov.in, select your state, and choose Apply for Learner Licence.

steps.title: Fill Form 2
steps.desc: Enter your details, vehicle class, and upload age and address proof.

steps.title: Pay and book
steps.desc: Pay the fee, then book the LL test slot, online from home in many states.

steps.title: Pass the test
steps.desc: Score 60% on the MCQ test on signs and rules, and the LL is issued the same day.

sections.heading: The Learner's Licence Process in Detail
content: Fill the LL form with your name, date of birth, and address as per Aadhaar, then select your vehicle class such as LMV for cars or MCWG for geared two-wheelers. Some states ask for a medical certificate, Form 1A.
The LL application fee is around Rs 150 to 200 per vehicle class, payable by UPI, net banking, or card. After payment you book the test slot.
The test is 15 to 20 MCQs on traffic rules and road signs, and you need 60% to pass. If you fail, you can retake after 7 days, so study the road signs chart first.
Some states like Delhi, Karnataka, and Maharashtra let you take the LL test online from home, while others require an RTO visit.
Once you pass, the LL is generated instantly as a digital copy you can download, or posted to you, depending on your state.
Use the free mock tests on the Parivahan portal to get familiar with the question format before your real LL test.
If you fail the LL test three times, you simply reapply, so there is no permanent block on getting your licence.

sections.heading: What You Can and Cannot Do on an LL
content: With an LL you may drive only with a permanent licence holder beside you, and with a red L displayed on the front and rear of the vehicle.
The LL is valid for 6 months, and you must convert it to a permanent DL within that window. If it expires first, you pay again for a fresh LL.
Common vehicle classes are LMV for cars and SUVs, MCWG for geared motorcycles, and MCWOG for gearless scooters. Heavy vehicles need separate training and a test.

sections.heading: Age Limits for Each Vehicle Type
content: You can get an LL for a gearless scooter up to 50cc at 16, with written parental consent. For geared two-wheelers and cars you must be at least 18.
For commercial and transport vehicles the minimum age is 20, with a year of light-vehicle experience and a medical certificate.
You must also be a resident of the state you apply in, and physically fit to drive, which the medical form confirms where required.
Minors below 18 can be issued a licence only for the gearless category, which converts to a full adult licence at 18.
Choosing the right vehicle class at the start saves a separate endorsement test later, so pick LMV, MCWG, or both as you need.

sections.heading: Step 2: Get Your Permanent Driving Licence

steps.title: Wait 30 days
steps.desc: Hold the LL for at least 30 days, using the time to practice driving.

steps.title: Apply with LL number
steps.desc: On Sarathi, choose Apply for Driving Licence and enter your LL number.

steps.title: Pay and book test
steps.desc: Pay the DL fee per vehicle class and book a driving test slot at your RTO.

steps.title: Pass the road test
steps.desc: Clear the practical test, and the DL is dispatched within 7 to 30 days.

sections.heading: The Driving Test, Step by Step
content: Use the 30-day gap to practice, since the permanent DL test is a practical road test, not theory. Practice with a licensed driver beside you, ideally on your RTO's own track.
On test day, carry your LL, Aadhaar, and the application receipt, and bring the vehicle you will drive. For a car test, arrange your own car unless your RTO provides one.
The test takes 10 to 15 minutes and covers forward driving, turns, reversing, and parking. If you fail, you can rebook after 7 days, with no limit on attempts.
For a two-wheeler test you usually ride a figure-8 track and navigate cones, showing signals and braking. For a car you start, drive forward, take turns, reverse, and parallel park.
Common fail reasons are hitting cones, stalling the engine, skipping indicators, and poor reversing. Smooth, controlled driving matters far more than speed.
If you stall the engine once, simply restart and continue, since a single stall is usually not an automatic failure.
Stay inside the marked lane throughout, because drifting outside it is one of the most common automatic-fail triggers.

sections.heading: What Fails You in the Driving Test
Are you ready to apply
qualify: You are 18 or older for a car or geared bike
You are 16+ with parental consent for a gearless scooter
You have Aadhaar and an address proof
You held your LL for at least 30 days
You have practised enough to pass the road test
disqualify: Below the minimum age for the vehicle class
LL is less than 30 days old or expired
No valid age or address proof
Applying through a tout instead of online
Bringing a test vehicle without valid RC or insurance

sections.heading: Documents You Need
content: For the LL, you need age proof such as Aadhaar showing 18+, an address proof, and a passport photo. A medical certificate, Form 1A, is needed for commercial classes or applicants over 40.
For the permanent DL, your valid LL plus the application receipt is the main requirement, since your other details are already on file.
To add a vehicle class later, like adding LMV to an existing two-wheeler licence, you apply for an endorsement and take only the new driving test, without resubmitting personal documents.
Your passport photo is often taken at the RTO during the test, which overrides any uploaded photo. Keep originals of all proofs for verification.
For a Heavy Motor Vehicle licence you must already hold an LMV licence for at least one year, then take a separate test with a heavy vehicle you arrange.

sections.heading: Document Checklist: LL vs Permanent DL
rows: Aadhaar best, if address changed then utility bill
Not needed for personal car/bike usually
Photo taken at RTO overrides any submitted photo

sections.heading: How to Pass the Test First Try

items.title: Practice on the RTO track
items.sub: Visit and rehearse the figure-8 and reverse parking days before.

items.title: Drive slow and smooth
items.sub: The test rewards control, not speed, so keep it calm.

items.title: Use mirrors and indicators
items.sub: Signal before every turn and check mirrors, even in reverse.

items.title: Avoid cones and boundaries
items.sub: Hitting a cone or crossing a line is an automatic fail in many RTOs.

sections.heading: Why People Fail, and How to Avoid It
content: The biggest reason for failure is too little practice, since the 30-day gap is meant for driving, not just waiting. Aim for 2 to 3 hours of practice daily near your RTO.
Forgetting indicators and mirrors is the next, and many RTOs treat this as an automatic fail. Build the habit during practice, not on test day.
Two-wheeler tests fail most on the figure-8, where a foot touches the ground. Car tests fail most on reverse and parallel parking, so drill both until they are second nature.
Your test vehicle must have valid RC, insurance, and a PUC certificate, or the test will not proceed even if you drive well.
Most people who fail the first time pass on the second or third attempt, so treat a fail as practice, not a setback.

sections.title: How Long Your DL Lasts
sections.desc:
A private driving licence is valid for 20 years, or until you turn 40 in most cases, whichever comes first. Some states extend this to age 50, so check yours.

After that it renews in 5-year cycles. A commercial licence is valid for only 5 years and renews each cycle.

sections.heading: Validity by Licence Category
rows: Example: DL issued at 25, valid until 45 (20 years) or 50 (age limit)
Must be renewed every 5 years. Medical cert required.
Age 60+: DL valid 1-3 years, then renew more frequently
Automatic conversion to adult DL at 18 (different validity)

sections.heading: Renewal, Duplicate, Address Change, and IDP
content: Renew on Sarathi up to a year before expiry, with a fee around Rs 200 and no driving test, only document and eye checks. Driving on an expired licence risks a Rs 5,000 fine.
For a lost or damaged DL, apply for a duplicate, which keeps the same number and validity. For a move, apply for an address change, which transfers the DL to the new RTO.
For driving abroad, get an International Driving Permit at your RTO for around Rs 1,000, valid for one year and accepted in 100-plus countries. Carry it with your Indian DL.
Renewal needs no driving test, only document verification and an eye test, and after 40 a Form 1A medical certificate is required.
While a duplicate is being processed, which takes 7 to 15 days, the digital DL in mParivahan works as valid proof. An address change to a new RTO jurisdiction transfers your DL there.
The International Driving Permit is accepted in over 100 countries under the Geneva and Vienna road traffic conventions.
Always carry both the IDP and your Indian DL together when driving abroad, since the IDP alone is not enough.

sections.heading: How to Renew Your DL

steps.title: Start a year before expiry
steps.description: Begin the renewal up to 12 months before your DL expires, so you never drive on a lapsed licence.

steps.title: Get Form 1A if you are 40+
steps.description: A medical certificate becomes mandatory once you cross 40 years of age.

steps.title: Apply and pay on Sarathi
steps.description: Choose DL Renewal, enter your DL number, fill the form, and pay the fee.

steps.title: Visit the RTO if asked
steps.description: Carry your original DL and confirmation for any final verification and eye test.

sections.heading: Commercial and Transport Vehicle Licences
content: A transport licence, or badge, is needed to drive taxis, autos, trucks, and buses. You must be at least 20, with a year of LMV experience and a Form 1A medical certificate.
For heavy vehicles, take formal training at a recognised HMV school first, which costs around Rs 5,000 to 15,000 for a 2 to 4 week course.
A fresh HMV transport licence can lead to truck or bus driving jobs paying Rs 15,000 to 30,000 a month, with Gulf driving roles paying far more. The licence and badge are the only real investment.
Several states have introduced special, often free or subsidised, permits for e-rickshaws to promote green transport. Check your state transport site for the rules.
An HMV licence is mandatory for trucks, buses, and any vehicle above 7,500 kg, and bus drivers may also need a conductor or PSV badge in some states.
Long-haul truck drivers and Gulf-country roles can earn far more than local driving, making the transport badge a genuine career step.
The badge plus the heavy-vehicle licence is the main cost, after which experience steadily raises your earning power.

sections.title: Skip the Agents, the Online Process Is Simple
sections.content:
Touts outside RTOs charge Rs 3,000 to 10,000 to process your DL. The online application takes about 30 minutes and costs only the official fee.

Everything is transparent online, so paying an agent only wastes money and can expose you to fraud.

sections.title: Keep Your DL on Your Phone with mParivahan
sections.content:
Download the mParivahan app and add your DL, which is legally valid for police checks and verification. You no longer need to carry the physical card.

The same digital DL is available in DigiLocker, so you always have a backup ready to show.

sections.text: 30 crore Indians hold a driving license - but an estimated 5 crore people drive without one. Driving without DL is a Rs 5,000 fine under the Motor Vehicles Amendment Act 2019. The application takes 30 minutes online, the LL test is 15 MCQs, and the driving test is 10 minutes. The entire process costs Rs 400-800. There's no excuse for driving without a license.

sections.heading: What It Costs and How Long It Takes
content: The learner's licence fee is roughly Rs 150 to 200 per class, and the permanent DL fee is similar, so a single-class licence often totals Rs 400 to 700.
The LL is issued the same day you pass the test. The permanent DL is dispatched within 7 to 30 days, while the digital copy is ready in mParivahan immediately.
Plan around the 30-day LL wait plus RTO slot availability, which can add 2 to 4 weeks, so the whole journey often takes about two months.
Adding an extra vehicle class later costs around Rs 200 to 300 and needs only the new driving test, not fresh documents.
Retaking a failed test after the 7-day wait usually costs a small retest fee, which varies by state.

sections.title: Official Sources and References
sections.content:
This page is based on the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and the Parivahan portal, verified against official notifications.

Since fees and slot rules vary slightly by state, always confirm details on sarathi.parivahan.gov.in for your own state before applying.

faqs.question: Do I need a lawyer or agent to get driving license?
faqs.answer:
NO. Entire process is online and free of agents.

LL costs ₹200, DL costs ₹400 - no extra charges. Agents charge ₹3,000-8,000 for something you can do yourself in 30 minutes.

Do it yourself online.

faqs.question: Can I get driving license without LL?
faqs.answer:
Not in most states. LL is mandatory - it's proof you know basic traffic rules.

Some states allow direct DL (without LL) for people over 40 - check your state's specific rule. Generally: LL first (30 days waiting) → Then DL.

faqs.question: I failed LL test (didn't score 60%). What now?
faqs.answer:
Retake after 7 days. There's no limit on LL test attempts as long as you're within the 6-month application validity.

Each retry: same ₹200 fee. Questions are similar - study traffic rules more and retake.

faqs.question: I haven't driven in years and LL expired. Do I reapply?
faqs.answer:
Yes. LL valid for 6 months.

If expired, apply for fresh LL again (₹200). Then wait 30 days, apply for DL.

The process repeats. It's better to apply for DL within 6 months of LL to avoid re-doing LL.

faqs.question: My DL is suspended/revoked due to driving under influence (DUI). Can I get it back?
faqs.answer:
Suspension: Temporary - usually 6-12 months. After suspension period, DL is automatically restored if no new violations.

Revocation: Permanent cancellation. To get new license, apply afresh (LL + DL, like a new person).

Check court order to see if it's suspension or revocation.

faqs.question: Can I drive in other states with my DL?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Indian DL is valid in ALL states.

You can drive anywhere in India. However, if you permanently move to a new state and want to change your address on DL, apply for address change at new state's RTO - LL is invalidated when you move states.

faqs.question: I lost my DL. How to get duplicate?
faqs.answer: Apply at your RTO: 'Duplicate DL' → Pay ₹200 fee → Upload ID proof → Process takes 10-15 days. Alternatively, download e-DL from DigiLocker (free, instant) if state has digitized DLs - e-DL is legally valid everywhere.

faqs.question: What is the minimum age for driving license in India?
faqs.answer:
16 years for MCWOG (motorcycle without gear - scooter, activa up to 50cc). 18 years for MCWG (motorcycle with gear) and LMV (car, jeep).

20 years for HMV (truck, bus) - must hold LMV for at least 1 year. For transport license (commercial driving): 20 years minimum with 8th pass education.

faqs.question: How much does driving license cost?
faqs.answer:
Learner's License: Rs 200 per vehicle class. Permanent DL: Rs 200-300 per class.

Smart card DL fee: Rs 200. Total for LL + DL for LMV + MCWG: approximately Rs 800-1,200.

Renewal: Rs 200. Duplicate: Rs 200.

International Driving Permit: Rs 1,000. All fees are paid online at parivahan.gov.in.

faqs.question: Can I apply for DL online without visiting RTO?
faqs.answer:
Learner's License: Yes - completely online in many states (Delhi, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu). The MCQ test is taken online from home.

Permanent DL: You must visit the RTO for the practical driving test - this cannot be done online. However, the application and appointment booking are all online.

faqs.question: What happens if I fail the driving test?
faqs.answer:
You can rebook the test after 7 days. There's no limit on attempts - you can retry as many times as needed within your LL validity (6 months).

Each re-test costs Rs 300 as re-test fee. If your LL expires before you pass the driving test, you'll need to apply for a fresh LL and start over.

Practice more between attempts - specifically the skills that caused failure.

faqs.question: What is the fee for a driving licence in India?
faqs.answer:
The learner's licence fee is around Rs 150 to 200 per vehicle class, and the permanent DL fee is similar. The total usually comes to Rs 200 to 700 depending on classes and state.

An International Driving Permit costs around Rs 1,000. Pay only the official fee online and avoid agents.

faqs.question: How many days after LL can I apply for permanent DL?
faqs.answer:
You must hold the learner's licence for at least 30 days before applying for the permanent driving licence. You also need to apply within 180 days, before the LL expires.

Use those 30 days to practice, since the permanent DL test is a practical road test.

faqs.question: How long is a driving licence valid?
faqs.answer:
A private driving licence is valid for 20 years, or until age 40 in most cases, whichever comes first. Some states extend this to age 50.

After that it renews in 5-year cycles. A commercial licence is valid for only 5 years.

disclaimer: Driving license procedures, fees, and validity as per Ministry of Road Transport guidelines as of March 2026. RTO practices vary by state - check your state RTO's website for exact procedures and requirements.
